text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
--- 75 percent of all Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) passengers choose SAS rather than competing airlines after signing up for SAS Euro Bonus discount deals, according to a survey by the airline.

--- Alleged misinformation to Copenhagen Stock Exchange and investors by the former Bikuben savings bank in connection with the sale of shares in now bankrupt leasing group Commercial Holding, could trigger 180-200 million crown claims. Bikuben merged with the post office's Giro Bank to form BG Bank in January 1996.
--- The acute shortage of qualified IT staff in Denmark is forcing a growing number of companies to offer rewards of up to 10,000 crowns to employees who can find new IT staff for them.

---If the European Commission's proposal to fix minimum rates for common energy taxes within the EU comes into effect, it could lead to higher energy taxes in Denmark as rates in some EU member states are above Danish levels.
--- Vietnam was the main beneficiary of Danish developmental aid in Asia last year and Denmark expects to grant some 220 million crowns to the country this year.
